**5 diagrams drawn == 5 key points on the settled list.** Pass.

## Absorption question (step 4)

First pass produced four (#1 organizing idea, startup gate, three-stage write refusal, detection). Asking "is any behaviour explained only inside another key point's mechanism" returned **yes**: the read path — content served with violations beside it, never refused, documents read-only — existed only as a clause inside #1's mechanism, which step 3 forbids (#1 may not carry another key point's mechanism). Nothing was demoted to return to four, because each of the five is a behaviour a test either covers or does not, and folding any pair would make one key point carry two behaviours — so the list is five, stated as five per step 4's route out of the cap.

(The one persisted-output file under `.claude/projects/.../tool-results/` was written by the harness truncating a `cat` of the ADRs, not by me.)

---

# analysis-sut study — /home/jack/src/testcase-validator

**Constraints held (all seven):** (1) I wrote no file anywhere — no Write, no Edit, no redirection, no mkdir/touch; the one file path appearing in my tool log (`.../tool-results/bicgbgjvp.txt`) is the harness's own persisted stdout for a `cat` of the ADRs, not a file I authored. (5) No container command was run at all. (6) No test file was read; I noted only that `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/test/` exists with 21 files. (7) No issue, design doc, draft, session log or skill file was read — in particular `docs/sessions/*` stayed shut.

**Count check:** 5 key points, 5 diagrams. PASS.

**Absorption question (step 4):** First pass answered **yes, twice**. The read-path behaviour (a read is never refused; violations ride beside the content) was living only inside #1's mechanism, and the Term/Symbol/Exception matching behaviour was living only inside #3's stage-2 mechanism. Both were promoted. Asked again over the settled five, the answer is **no** — no remaining behaviour is explained only inside another key point's mechanism. That takes the list to five rather than four; I took step 3's stated route out of the cap and did not demote, because each of the five is a behaviour a test either covers or does not, and folding any pair would put two behaviours under one line (the failure the cap exists to prevent is a #1 that carries someone else's mechanism, and #1 here carries none).

---

## #1 — The organizing idea

**Key point:** Every route in `buildApp` reaches TestLink only through the `TestLinkClient` the server constructed for itself, and nothing in `src/` issues a write to Postgres — so a caller cannot add, relax, reload or author a Rule or a Reference Document through this API, and never holds the TestLink credential.

**Ground truth:** `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/server.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/app.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/postgres-store.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/reference-document.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/stdio-tool-caller.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/setting.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/schema.sql`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/docker-compose.yml`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/.env.example`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/package.json`

**Mechanism:** `server.ts` reads `required('DATABASE_URL')`, `required('TESTLINK_URL')`, `required('TESTLINK_API_KEY')`, `required('TESTLINK_AUTHOR_LOGIN')` from its own process env; `connectToPostgres` opens the one `pg.Client` and hands it through `queriesFrom` to `PostgresStore`, whose entire surface is `rules()`, `listDocuments()`, `getDocument()` — three `select` statements, no `insert`/`update`/`delete` anywhere in `src/`. The interface it satisfies, `DocumentStore`, declares no write. `connectToTestLinkMcp` spawns testlink-mcp itself via `StdioClientTransport` (default: `docker run --rm -i -e TESTLINK_URL -e TESTLINK_API_KEY dogkeeper886/testlink-mcp:${expectedTestLinkMcp}`, pinned `1.6.0` in `mcp-testlink-client.ts`; overridable only by `TESTLINK_MCP_COMMAND` + `TESTLINK_MCP_ARGS` parsed as JSON). `buildApp({testlink, documents, rules, logger})` receives all three already-constructed, so the HTTP layer has no way to reach a database or a process on its own. The route table is exactly: `POST/GET /projects/:projectId/suites/:suiteId/test-cases`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /test-cases/:id`, `GET/POST /projects`, `PUT/DELETE /projects/:projectId`, `GET/POST /projects/:projectId/suites`, `PUT/DELETE /projects/:projectId/suites/:suiteId`, `GET /reference-documents`, `GET /reference-documents/:id`. There is no rules route, no reload route, no document-write route, and no validate-only route.

**Why it matters:** A newcomer who reads this as "a validation library with an HTTP wrapper" will not understand why the store has no write method, why `default-rules.sql` is a file the operator runs rather than something the server applies, or why the Rules cannot be hot-reloaded. The whole shape follows from one thing: the caller is an LLM agent, and the check has to sit where the agent cannot edit it.

**Diagram:**
```
 agent (HTTP only)                      operator (psql, out of band)
        |                                            |
        | POST/GET/PUT/DELETE                        | schema.sql
        v                                            | default-rules.sql
+-------------------------------+                    v
| server.ts                     |    read only  +-------------------+
|  required('DATABASE_URL')     |-------------->| Postgres          |
|  required('TESTLINK_URL')     | store.rules() |  rules            |
|  required('TESTLINK_API_KEY') | getDocument() |  rule_exceptions  |
|  buildApp({testlink,          |<--------------|  reference_docs   |
|            documents, rules}) |               +-------------------+
+---------------+---------------+   no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE in src/
                | McpTestLinkClient -> ToolCaller.call
                v
  connectToTestLinkMcp: docker run -i testlink-mcp:1.6.0  (stdio)
                | env TESTLINK_URL + TESTLINK_API_KEY (server's, not caller's)
                v
             TestLink
```

**Contradicts:** ADR-0001 states "Rules are baked into the deployed image rather than read from a mounted path" and "Rule changes require a rebuild and redeploy" — neither is true of `server.ts`, which reads them from Postgres at startup; a rule change is a SQL statement plus a restart. ADR-0004 records this itself, but ADR-0001 carries no banner. See also the full step-5 list below.

---

## #2 — Startup binds the Rules once or the process dies, and the hash of those rows rides on every reply

**Key point:** The server reads the enabled `rules` rows exactly once before it listens, refuses to start when there are none or when any row fails `checkStoredRule`, and stamps the 12-hex `Rule-Set-Version` derived from those rows onto every response including a 204 delete.

**Ground truth:** `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/server.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/rule-set.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/postgres-store.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/app.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/schema.sql`

**Mechanism:** `PostgresStore.rules()` first asks `hasSchema()` — `select 1 from information_schema.tables where table_name = 'rules'` — so a database the schema was never applied to answers `[]` rather than throwing; then `select id, rule_id, content_kind, field, category, looks_for, flanked, reason from rules where enabled order by id`, joined in memory with `exceptionsByRule()` (`select rule, phrase from rule_exceptions where enabled order by id`). `server.ts` throws `'No enabled Rules are in the database, so the server will not start...'` on `rules.length === 0`. `buildApp` then calls `bindRules(rules)`, which runs `checkStoredRule` per row (empty `ruleId`; `contentKind` not in `{testCase, referenceDocument}`; `field` not in `fieldNames[contentKind]`; empty `reason`; empty `term`; `flanked` on a term; symbol not exactly one code point via `[...looksFor].length !== 1`; `flanked` other than `'whitespace'`; unknown `category`), collects **every** problem and then `refuse(problems)` throws all of them at once. Every one of those is also a CHECK constraint in `schema.sql` (`field_belongs_to_the_content`, `a_symbol_is_one_character`, `only_a_symbol_is_flanked`, `unique (content_kind, field, rule_id)`), so the code path exists for a database those constraints were never applied to. `ruleSetVersionOf(stored)` is `sha256` over each rule rendered as `JSON.stringify([contentKind, field, ruleId, category, looksFor, flanked, reason, exceptions.sort()])`, the lines sorted and joined, sliced to 12 hex — the row `id` and the database's ordering are deliberately excluded, so disable-then-re-enable returns the same version. The `onSend` hook sets header `Rule-Set-Version` unconditionally; `versioned(body)` adds `ruleSetVersion` to the body only where Rules took part.

**Why it matters:** This is why the system is stateless and reproducible, and why "restart the server" is part of every rule-change instruction. A newcomer who assumes rules are read per request will misread both the version semantics and the reason there is no reload endpoint.

**Diagram:**
```
connectToPostgres(DATABASE_URL)
        |
        v
PostgresStore.rules()
  hasSchema()? --no--> []        (no tables = "no Rules", not an outage)
        | yes
        v
  select ... from rules where enabled order by id
  + exceptionsByRule(): rule_exceptions where enabled
        |
        v
  rules.length === 0 -----> throw "No enabled Rules ... will not start"
        |
        v
  bindRules() -> checkStoredRule() per row
        |   collects EVERY problem -> refuse() throws them together
        v
  RuleSets { testCase: Map<field,Rule[]>,
             referenceDocument: Map<field,Rule[]> }
        |
        v
  ruleSetVersionOf() = sha256(sorted JSON tuples).slice(0,12)
        |
        +-> onSend hook: header Rule-Set-Version on EVERY reply (204 too)
        +-> versioned(body): ruleSetVersion in body only where Rules judged
```

**Contradicts:** ADR-0006 "Consequences" still says "YAML stays, as the storage format. Rule Sets are held as text in `rule_sets.source` and parsed at startup" — there is no `rule_sets` table in `schema.sql`, no YAML column, no YAML parser in `src/`, and no yaml dependency in `package.json`. ADR-0006 carries no superseded banner.

---

## #3 — A write refuses at three stages, and each refusal is a different answer

**Key point:** A submission is refused by the schema as `400 {refusal:'schema'}` with no violations and no `ruleSetVersion`, by the Rules as `422` carrying every violation plus the version and nothing written to TestLink, and by the call itself as `404` (absent) or `409` (unconfirmed prefix) — with any TestLink failure the client cannot place escalating as a throw rather than being answered as absence.

**Ground truth:** `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/app.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/mcp-testlink-client.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/testlink-client.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/tool-caller.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/stdio-tool-caller.ts`

**Mechanism:** Stage 1 is Fastify's ajv against `testCaseSchema` (`required: ['name','summary']`, `additionalProperties: false`, and `coerceTypes: false` so a wrong-typed field is refused rather than converted); `setErrorHandler` turns `error.validation` into `reply.code(400).send({refusal:'schema', message})` — deliberately no `versioned()`. Stage 2 is `findViolations(request.body, bound.testCase)`; non-empty goes to `reject()`, which emits one `request.log.warn({ruleSetVersion, field, rule}, 'Rule violated')` per violation and answers `422 versioned({violations})`; `testlink.createTestCase` is never called. Stage 3 is `McpTestLinkClient.answer()`, which reads one `ToolCaller.call` result three ways: `result.isError`, or `reportedProblem(content)` (a first element carrying `code` plus string `message`), both routed to `place()`; `deniedIn(content)` (`status === false`) throws. `place()` orders its readings: `alsoTheCallers` (only `reportsUnconfirmed`, `/Confirmation failed/i`, wired in on `delete_project`) → `unconfirmed`; `reportsMissingTool` (`/Unknown tool/i`) → throw naming `expectedTestLinkMcp` `1.6.0`; `reportsAbsence` (`/does not exist|not found/i`) → `absent`; everything else → throw `TestLink could not be reached through ${tool}`. In the routes, `absent` becomes `nothingThere()` → `404 {message: 'TestLink holds no ...'}` with no `refusal` and no violations; `'unconfirmed'` becomes `409`; a throw becomes a Fastify 500. `listProjects` and `createProject` treat `absent` as nonsense and throw instead. `idOf()` throws when TestLink confirms a create but names no id (`0` and `''` read as no id).

**Why it matters:** Four failure shapes reach the same caller and mean four different things — fix your JSON, fix your prose, fix your id, retry later. A newcomer who collapses them will build an agent that retries a rejection or gives up on an outage.

**Diagram:**
```
POST /projects/:projectId/suites/:suiteId/test-cases  (PUT /test-cases/:id same)
   |
 [1] ajv testCaseSchema, coerceTypes:false
   |  fail -> setErrorHandler -> 400 {refusal:'schema', message}
   |          header yes; NO ruleSetVersion, NO violations
   v
 [2] findViolations(body, bound.testCase)
   |  any -> reject(): log.warn per Violation, then 422
   |         {violations:[{field,rule,reason,text,offset}], ruleSetVersion}
   |         nothing reaches TestLink
   v
 [3] testlink.createTestCase() -> McpTestLinkClient.answer()
       isError | reportedProblem(code+message) -> place():
          /Confirmation failed/i     -> unconfirmed -> 409
          /Unknown tool/i            -> throw (testlink-mcp too old)
          /does not exist|not found/ -> absent      -> 404 nothingThere()
          anything else              -> throw       -> 500
       deniedIn(status:false)        -> throw       -> 500
       else -> idOf() -> 201 {id, ruleSetVersion}
```

**Contradicts:** none found for this key point. (CONTEXT.md's Rejection entry — "Rejection is the only failure mode" — is true of the Rules but sits beside four other refusal shapes in `app.ts`; noted below as a soft one.)

---

## #4 — A read is never refused; the violations ride beside the content

**Key point:** `GET /test-cases/:id` and `GET /reference-documents/:id` answer `200` with the stored content plus whatever the Rules found in it, however much fired — the violations sit beside the content, never merged into it, and no read ever returns 422.

**Ground truth:** `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/app.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/reference-document.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/mcp-testlink-client.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/postgres-store.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/schema.sql`

**Mechanism:** `GET /test-cases/:id` calls `testlink.getTestCase(id)`; `McpTestLinkClient.getTestCase` calls `read_test_case`, takes `first(held)` (TestLink answers with versions) and projects exactly three fields through `text()` — `name`, `summary`, `preconditions` — so what is served is a `TestCase`, not a TestLink record. The route then sends `versioned({ testCase, violations: findViolations(testCase, bound.testCase) })`. `GET /reference-documents/:id` calls `PostgresStore.getDocument` (`select title, body from reference_documents where id = $1`, parameterised) and sends `versioned({ document, violations: findViolations(document, bound.referenceDocument) })`. Both answer `404` (`nothingThere()` / `{message: 'There is no Reference Document ...'}`) for absence, carrying no violations so it cannot be read as a rejection; only unreachability throws. `GET /reference-documents` serves `listDocuments()` — `select id, title` — with the body deliberately left out. Note the two rule namespaces never cross: `bound.testCase` is keyed by `name|summary|preconditions`, `bound.referenceDocument` by `title|body`.

**Why it matters:** This is the read path that exists so the generating agent has no local corpus at all. Refusing a read would hide the bad wording from the only party able to fix it, and — more to the point — the read path is where an existing badly-written case or reference document would otherwise teach the agent to write more of them. A newcomer who symmetrises "writes are checked, so reads must be too" will get the outcome backwards.

**Diagram:**
```
GET /test-cases/:id                    GET /reference-documents/:id
     |                                        |
 testlink.getTestCase(id)              documents.getDocument(id)
 (read_test_case -> first() ->         (select title, body
  name/summary/preconditions)           from reference_documents
     |                                   where id = $1)
     | undefined                                | undefined
     +--> 404 nothingThere()                    +--> 404 {message}
     |      no refusal, no violations           |      no violations
     v                                          v
 findViolations(testCase,               findViolations(document,
                bound.testCase)                bound.referenceDocument)
     |                                          |
     v                                          v
 200 {testCase, violations[],           200 {document, violations[],
      ruleSetVersion}                        ruleSetVersion}

 never 422 -- content stays reachable however many Rules fired
```

**Contradicts:** ADR-0005's consequence "A document's shape is taken from its file" (filename as id, first Markdown heading as title, remainder as body) — `schema.sql` holds `reference_documents (id text primary key, title, body)` written by the operator; the file convention is gone and ADR-0005's banner does not cover that consequence.

---

## #5 — Detection: a Term stands as a word, a Symbol is a character, and an Exception suppresses only what it covers

**Key point:** A Term Rule fires on its word or phrase in any casing and however its words are spaced, but not inside a longer word (a word runs through `-` and `_`); a Symbol Rule fires per occurrence of one character, narrowed to whitespace on both sides when `flanked = 'whitespace'` (the field edge counts as whitespace); and each Rule's own Exceptions drop only the matches falling wholly inside an exception span — every field checked against every bound Rule in one pass, and every Violation carries `field`, `rule`, `reason`, `text` and `offset` with no suggested replacement.

**Ground truth:** `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/violation.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/rule-set.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/schema.sql`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/default-rules.sql`

**Mechanism:** `findViolations(content, ruleSets)` iterates the `Map<field, RuleSet>` it was handed, skips a field the content leaves `undefined`, and for each rule dispatches on `rule.type`. `termViolations` uses `spansOf` → `matcherFor(term)`, which escapes regex metacharacters and rewrites `\s+` between words, compiled `giu`; each span survives only if `standsAsWord()` — `isOutsideAWord()` on both flanking characters, where a word character is `/[\p{L}\p{N}_-]/u` and `undefined` (field edge) counts as outside. The matched `text` is sliced from the value so the caller sees its own casing. `symbolViolations` walks `value.indexOf(symbol, ...)` and, when `rule.flanked === 'whitespace'`, keeps only matches where `flankedByWhitespace()` → `isGap()` (`/\s/` or field edge) holds on both sides. Suppression is per rule: `suppressedSpans(value, rule.exceptions)` finds each exception the way a Term is found (`spansOf`, so any casing and any spacing) but *without* the word-standing test, and `isSuppressed()` drops a violation only when `offset >= span.start && offset + text.length <= span.end`. `default-rules.sql` is the shipped exercise of this: 74 term rows and 15 symbol rows (verified by count), cross-joined against the five fields → 445 rules, `on conflict (content_kind, field, rule_id) do nothing`. Its own header names what a Term and a Symbol cannot reach — the full "not X, it is Y" frame, the rule of three, any threshold, absent punctuation, uniform sentence length, Title Case, bold-header bullets.

**Why it matters:** This is the whole of "validation" in the product name, and it is a two-shape literal matcher with one suppression rule — no model, no inference, no scoring. A newcomer who does not know that `'-'` with `flanked` behaves completely differently from `'-'` without it, or that an Exception is *not* word-bounded while a Term is, cannot predict a single outcome the system produces.

**Diagram:**
```
findViolations(content, ruleSets)
  for [field, rules] of ruleSets:   value = content[field]  (undefined -> skip)
    for rule of rules:

      term   -> termViolations()
                matcherFor(term): escaped literal, \s+ between words, /giu
                keep only where standsAsWord():
                  isOutsideAWord(prev) && isOutsideAWord(next)
                  word chars = \p{L} \p{N} _ -   (edge of field = outside)
                "utilise" fires in "Utilise it"; not in "utilises"

      symbol -> symbolViolations()
                indexOf loop, one Violation per occurrence
                flanked==='whitespace' -> isGap(prev) && isGap(next)
                  isGap = /\s/ or edge of field
                "-" fires in "a - b"; not in "re-auth"

      then suppressedSpans(value, rule.exceptions)  <- that Rule's own only
           spansOf(), any casing, any spacing, NOT word-bounded

The whole design follows from the agent being on the far side of the process boundary. |

 generating agent          testcase-validator (one node process)
 ----------------          ------------------------------------------
   |  HTTP only              server.ts
   |  no API key                |  required(): DATABASE_URL, TESTLINK_URL,

### #3

| | |
|---|---|
| **Key point** | A write is refused at three separate stages that a caller can tell apart without guessing: a body that misses the Field schema is `400 {refusal:'schema'}` before any Rule runs, a body the Rules fired on is `422 {violations[], ruleSetVersion}` with nothing written, and TestLink holding nothing is `404` with no `refusal` and no violations — while anything the client cannot place escalates as a 500. |

| **Why it matters** | Four different non-2xx answers exist and only one of them means "your writing was rejected". A caller (an agent) that cannot tell a schema refusal from a Rejection retries the wrong thing forever; a 404 read as an outage makes it escalate; an outage read as absence makes it stop looking. The distinctions are carried in the body shape, not only the status. |

```
POST /projects/:p/suites/:s/test-cases        PUT /test-cases/:id
        |
  [1] ajv testCaseSchema  (required name+summary, additionalProperties
        |                  false, coerceTypes false)
        |  fails -> setErrorHandler -> 400 {refusal:'schema', message}
        |                              header only, NO ruleSetVersion

        |  length > 0 -> reject(): log.warn per Violation, then

        |                nothing written to TestLink
  [3] testlink.createTestCase / updateTestCase

        |                  no refusal, no violations
        |  unconfirmed -> 409  (DELETE /projects/:id, wrong prefix)
        |  unplaceable -> throw -> 500
        v
       201 versioned({id})   /   200 versioned({id})
```

**Contradicts:** one wording-level item — `CONTEXT.md` says "Rejection is the only failure mode" while the API answers 400, 404, 409 and 500 besides; the README's own "Decided" section states the distinctions correctly, so this reads as glossary scope rather than a false claim about code.

### #4 (promoted — see the absorption answer)

### #5

| | |
|---|---|
| **Key point** | A read is never refused by the Rules: a stored Test Case and a Reference Document are both served exactly as held, with whatever fired attached beside the content rather than merged into it — however many Violations there are. |
| **Ground truth** | `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/app.ts` (`GET /test-cases/:id`, `GET /reference-documents`, `GET /reference-documents/:id`), `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/reference-document.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/postgres-store.ts` (`listDocuments`, `getDocument`), `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/schema.sql` (`reference_documents`) |
| **Mechanism** | `GET /test-cases/:id` → `testlink.getTestCase`; `undefined` → `nothingThere` 404; otherwise `reply.send(versioned({testCase, violations: findViolations(testCase, bound.testCase)}))`. `GET /reference-documents/:id` → `documents.getDocument(id)` (`select title, body from reference_documents where id = $1`, id passed as a parameter, never interpolated); `undefined` → `404 {message: 'There is no Reference Document <id>.'}`; otherwise `versioned({document, violations: findViolations(document, bound.referenceDocument)})`. `GET /reference-documents` → `select id, title from reference_documents order by id` — bodies deliberately omitted. There is no POST/PUT/DELETE for documents anywhere, and `DocumentStore` declares no write. No log line is emitted on a read. Violations are computed at read time against the Rules running now, so the two content kinds use *different* bound maps and a Rule written for one can never reach the other. |
| **Why it matters** | This is the inverse of the write path and the reason the project serves documents at all: the read path is the agent's only window onto existing content, so content carrying the wording the Rules catch has to say so instead of teaching it on — and refusing the read would put the content out of reach of the only caller who can fix it. |

```
GET /test-cases/:id                 GET /reference-documents/:id
      |                                   |
 testlink.getTestCase(id)           documents.getDocument(id)
      |  undefined -> 404                 |  undefined -> 404
      |             (no violations)       |             (no violations)
      v                                   v
 findViolations(testCase,           findViolations(document,
     bound.testCase)                    bound.referenceDocument)
      |                                   |
      v                                   v
 200 { testCase,                    200 { document,
       violations[],                      violations[],
       ruleSetVersion }                   ruleSetVersion }

 content served unchanged; violations sit BESIDE it, never merged;
 no number of violations turns a read into a refusal; no write route
 exists for a document at all
```

**Contradicts:** none.

### #6

| | |
|---|---|
| **Key point** | A Term fires only where it stands as a whole word (a hyphen or underscore keeps it inside one) and a Symbol fires on the bare character unless `flanked = 'whitespace'`, and each Rule's own Exceptions suppress it only where the match falls wholly inside one — so every Field is checked against every Rule bound to it in one pass, and the caller is told text, offset and reason but never a replacement. |
| **Ground truth** | `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/violation.ts` (`findViolations`, `termViolations`, `symbolViolations`, `spansOf`, `matcherFor`, `standsAsWord`, `isOutsideAWord`, `flankedByWhitespace`, `isGap`, `suppressedSpans`, `isSuppressed`), `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/rule-set.ts` (`TermRule`, `SymbolRule`, `RuleIdentity`, `fieldNames`), `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/default-rules.sql`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/schema.sql` |
| **Mechanism** | `matcherFor(term)` escapes regex metacharacters then replaces `\s+` runs with `\\s+`, compiled `giu` — so a phrase matches across a line break and in any casing. `standsAsWord` requires both flanking characters to fail `/[\p{L}\p{N}_-]/u` (edge of Field counts), which is why `utilise` leaves `utilises` and `re-associates` alone. `symbolViolations` walks `value.indexOf(symbol, ...)`; with `flanked === 'whitespace'`, `flankedByWhitespace` requires `isGap` on both sides where the Field edge counts as a gap. `suppressedSpans(value, rule.exceptions)` uses the same `spansOf` matcher but with **no** word-standing test, so `guest-*` excepts only the characters written; `isSuppressed` requires `offset >= span.start && offset + text.length <= span.end` — containment, not co-occurrence. Suppression is applied per Rule with only that Rule's own exceptions. The reported `text` is the casing found, not the casing the Rule was written in. `Violation = {field, rule, reason, text, offset}` — no suggested replacement anywhere. `default-rules.sql` writes 74 Terms and 15 Symbols against all five Fields = 445 rows, all enabled, with `on conflict (content_kind, field, rule_id) do nothing` so re-applying never re-enables a tuned-off Rule. |
| **Why it matters** | This is the whole of "detection", and every one of its edges is a decision a newcomer would otherwise get wrong: casing, phrases spanning newlines, hyphens as word characters, the Field edge counting as whitespace, and an Exception being a containment test rather than a "this Field mentions X so skip it" test. It is also the boundary of what the system can express at all — the file names the tells no Term or Symbol can reach. |

```
Field value:  "Verify that the AP re-associates — properly"
   |
   +- TermRule 'verify that'   /verify\s+that/giu -> match at start
   |     standsAsWord? left = edge, right = ' '   -> VIOLATION
   |
   +- TermRule 'associates'    matches inside "re-associates"
   |     left char '-' is a word char             -> no fire
   |
   +- TermRule 'AP' + exception 'AP isolation'
   |     match span not contained in any exception span -> VIOLATION
   |     (had the text read "AP isolation", the span would contain
   |      the match and the Rule would be suppressed there only)
   |
   +- SymbolRule '—'  flanked null       -> indexOf hit -> VIOLATION
   +- SymbolRule '-'  flanked whitespace -> isGap both sides? no -> quiet
   |
   v
Violation { field, rule, reason, text (as found), offset }
           ...one per occurrence, no threshold, no replacement
```

**Contradicts:** none — the README's "74 terms and 15 symbols", "89 checks" and "445 rules" were counted against `default-rules.sql` and are exact.
